solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Changing Text Case in MS Word**

**Definition:** In Microsoft Word, changing the case of selected text involves altering the capitalization of the letters in the text. This can be done quickly and easily using various methods, each suited to different user preferences and scenarios.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 1: Use the keyboard shortcut ‘Shift + F3’**

This option correctly describes a quick and efficient method to change the case of selected text in MS Word. When you select a portion of text and press the ‘Shift + F3’ keyboard shortcut, it cycles through three different case options: all uppercase, all lowercase, and capitalizing the first letter of each word (also known as Title Case).

**Detailed Explanation:**

Using ‘Shift + F3’ is one of the most convenient ways to change text case in MS Word. Here is a step-by-step process:

 
• **Select the Text:** Highlight the text you want to change the case of. This can be done by clicking and dragging your mouse over the text, or by using the keyboard shortcut ‘Ctrl + A’ to select all the text in the document.
 
• **Press ‘Shift + F3’:** Hold down the ‘Shift’ key and press the ‘F3’ key. Each time you press this combination, the case of the selected text will change:
 __
 
• **First Press:** Changes the text to all uppercase letters (e.g., "THIS IS AN EXAMPLE").
 
• **Second Press:** Changes the text to all lowercase letters (e.g., "this is an example").
 
• **Third Press:** Changes the text to Title Case, where the first letter of each word is capitalized (e.g., "This Is An Example").
 
 

This method is highly efficient because it allows users to quickly switch between different cases without navigating through menus or using the mouse, which can save time and increase productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

To further understand the analysis, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 2: Right-click the selected text and choose ‘Font’**

This option is not the quickest method for changing text case. Right-clicking the selected text and choosing ‘Font’ opens the Font dialog box, which allows you to change various font properties such as typeface, size, color, and effects, but it does not provide an option to change the text case directly. Therefore, this method is incorrect for the purpose of changing text case quickly.

**Option 3: Change it manually by typing the text again**

This option is the least efficient and is not practical for quickly changing text case. Manually retyping the text in the desired case is time-consuming and prone to errors, especially for larger sections of text. This method is not recommended when quicker and more efficient alternatives are available.

**Option 4: Go to the ‘Home’ tab and click on ‘Change Case’**

This option is a valid method for changing text case, but it is not as quick as using the keyboard shortcut ‘Shift + F3’. Here is how you would use this method:

 
• Select the text you want to change.
 
• Navigate to the ‘Home’ tab in the ribbon.
 
• Click on the ‘Change Case’ button in the ‘Font’ group.
 
• Choose from the available case options: Sentence case, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalize Each Word, or tOGGLE cASE.

 

While this method is effective, it requires more steps and mouse clicks compared to the keyboard shortcut, making it slightly less efficient.

**Conclusion:**

Understanding the different methods for changing text case in MS Word is essential for choosing the most efficient approach based on the user's needs. The ‘Shift + F3’ keyboard shortcut is the quickest and most efficient method for changing the case of selected text, cycling through uppercase, lowercase, and Title Case with ease. While other methods such as using the ‘Change Case’ button in the ‘Home’ tab are also effective, they are not as quick and convenient as the keyboard shortcut. Manual retyping should be avoided due to its inefficiency and potential for errors.
